steps.what: List items below the stored minimum
Order and purchase equipment and supplies
Check the price before the order
Sign the purchase order
Place only the signed purchase order
outputs: filed copy of signed purchase order v1

tasks.design: A job lists items in {PROCUREMENT} below the stored minimum. The manager decides the equipment or supplies and checks the price. A later job places only that signed order. It does not buy an unsigned line.
tasks.previous_blocker: Short items were copied before the order was written.
tasks.enabler_now: Item identifier, quantity, minimum, and price are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The manager still chooses what to buy.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the order, not on finding short items.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says budgets and records come from the booking or ledger system, and a person checks the commentary against the figures.

assumptions: Item identifier, quantity, minimum, and price are stored on the purchasing record. The purchasing record produces them. An item is listed only when the quantity is below the minimum. A blank minimum is shown as not short. A blank price is not ordered.
Native configuration of the purchasing record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining choice is still the manager ordering the supplies.

incremental.description: Refresh item identifier, quantity, minimum, and price when the purchasing layout changes, and drop an order the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many minimums or prices are blank. The high end assumes item identifier, minimum, and price are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List stored operational problem rows
Review work procedures and operational problems
Determine ways to improve safety
Sign the improvement note
File the signed improvement note
outputs: filed copy of signed improvement note v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored operational problems in {DOCS}. The manager reviews the work procedures and determines ways to improve service, performance, or safety. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}. It does not score a person, and it does not draft the note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Problems were pasted into a fresh note each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Problem identifier and area are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The improvement is still the manager's judgement.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the review, not on collecting problems.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says strategy and people work stay manual.
Digest [S15] says a model-drafted review cited sources that were not real. This design does not draft the commentary.
Digest [S10] says hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk.

assumptions: Problem identifier, area, and date are stored on the document record. The document record produces them. A blank area stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the document record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
Service performance here is the operation, not a score of a named person.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining review is still the manager reviewing the procedures.

incremental.description: Refresh problem identifier and area when the document layout changes, and drop a note the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many problem areas are blank. The high end assumes problem identifier and area are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List equipment due by maintenance interval
Arrange equipment maintenance and repairs
Coordinate waste removal and pest control
Sign the service order
Place only the signed service order
outputs: filed copy of signed service order v1

tasks.design: A job lists equipment in {OPS_SYSTEM} that is due because the stored maintenance interval has passed. The manager arranges the repair and coordinates waste removal or pest control. A later job places only that signed order in {PROCUREMENT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Due equipment was copied before the call.
tasks.enabler_now: Asset identifier, interval, and last service date are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The manager still chooses the service.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week arranging the service, not on finding due assets.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says budgets and records come from the booking or ledger system, and a person checks the commentary against the figures.

assumptions: Asset identifier, maintenance interval, and last service date are stored on the operations record. The operations record produces them. An asset is due when the interval has passed since the last service date. A blank interval is shown as not due.
Native configuration of the operations record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining arrangement is still the manager arranging the repair.

incremental.description: Refresh asset identifier, interval, and last service date when the operations layout changes, and drop an order the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes the maintenance interval is often blank. The high end assumes asset identifier, interval, and last service date are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Watch the floor for liquor rules.

steps.what: List the stored liquor service rules
Monitor employee and patron activities
Judge whether liquor regulations were obeyed
Sign the floor note
File the signed floor note
outputs: filed copy of signed floor note v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored liquor service rules in {DOCS}. The manager monitors employee and patron activities in person and judges whether the regulations were obeyed. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}. It does not watch the floor with a camera and it does not log named staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rule text was copied before the shift.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule identifier and rule text are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The floor is still watched by the manager.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides whether the rule was obeyed.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the floor, not on finding the rule text.

reach.task: Read only the signed floor note

evidence.claim: The executive digest says strategy and people work stay manual.
Digest [S12] says rosters and staff monitoring need works-council consent.

assumptions: Rule identifier and rule text are stored on the document record. The document record produces them. A blank rule stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the document record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
Works-council consent for a roster or for monitoring named staff is a separate decision. This design does not treat that consent as already given, and it does not build a camera score of patrons.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining watch is still the manager monitoring the floor.

incremental.description: Refresh rule identifier and rule text when the document layout changes, and drop a note the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many rule texts are blank. The high end assumes rule identifier and rule text are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The food service manager spends the week on the floor, the guest, and the signed decision. A stored total, a working-time slot with no name, and filing that decision can move. The manager still counts the cash, tastes the food, and assigns the names.
reach: A cook follows only the assignment the manager signed.
A supplier receives only the order the manager signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a roster slot that already contains a person name.
Reject a total that does not match the stored rows.
Reject an order that the manager has not signed.
role.ambitious_version: A signed roster or order can be filed the same week, and the manager still owns the floor.
